html:
The escalating confrontation between the United States and Iran has reached a critical point, with President Donald Trump threatening an imminent military strike on Iran's "Pickaxe Mountain" and reports indicating Iranian missiles were intercepted over Jordan, prompting defense system activation in Kuwait. The US has already launched fresh attacks on military targets in Iran, with Trump stating the aim is to prevent Tehran from rebuilding destroyed capabilities.

US-Iran: The prospect of direct military engagement between the US and Iran intensifies, following President Trump's explicit warning of a potential attack. This comes as Netanyahu states that toppling Iran's regime is "within reach," and Iran's ambassador to Egypt asserts that adherence to Iran's conditions must precede the opening of the Strait of Hormuz or any negotiations with Washington. Gulf shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is reported to be below its 10-day average. Furthermore, China has banned the enforcement of US oil sanctions, while Trump has also floated the idea of renaming the Strait of Hormuz to "Trump Strait."

Russia-Ukraine & European Security: Russia has intensified its air war against Ukraine, striking Ukrainian security headquarters in Kyiv with drones, which Zelensky says hit without warning. Reports describe this as the most intense wave of attacks on the Ukrainian capital in four years. Meanwhile, President Trump's peace envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, are scheduled to visit Moscow and Kyiv over the weekend in an effort to end the conflict, though talks have stalled. Europe is facing a spiralling campaign of sabotage, with Russia identified as the chief suspect, following Germany's blame on Russia for an attack on Leipzig airport, though the German Interior Minister has also linked some power grid sabotage to militant climate activists. Norway has seized a Russian ship in Svalbard to compensate Ukraine, drawing protests from Russia.

US Politics & Global Economy: President Trump has re-engaged his fight with the Federal Reserve, threatening to halt trade with countries that maintain a trade deficit with the US unless the central bank lowers interest rates, citing August's strong jobs report as justification. In economic news, diesel prices have reached a record high, and the head of Iraq's Energy Center warned that oil prices could reach $100 per barrel. Separately, Uber has withdrawn from Nigeria and Uganda, leaving thousands of drivers seeking new income sources.

Israel-Palestine & Regional Dynamics: The United States has rejected Israeli suggestions regarding the removal of Palestinians from Gaza, with the State Department affirming Washington "does not support any plan" for their expulsion. This follows extremist Israeli minister Ben Gvir presenting a plan to remove Palestinians from Gaza. A UN report warned that Israel's forced displacement of populations from three West Bank refugee camps could amount to crimes against humanity, as Israeli forces continue to demolish Palestinian homes in the West Bank. An Israeli drone strike in southern Lebanon killed two people, which the IDF stated was a response to a Hezbollah explosive drone launch.

Global Governance & Other Events: The United Nations General Assembly has voted to adopt a new world map to reflect Africa's true size, with 164 nations backing the resolution, while the US was the only nation to vote against it. In South America, President Javier Milei of Argentina is escalating a dispute with Britain over the Falkland Islands, imposing tougher sanctions, with President Trump suggesting he might support Milei's drive to reclaim the islands as "revenge on the UK." In Nepal, rescue efforts continue after devastating floods knocked out over 10% of the country's energy generation capacity, with two workers successfully rescued from a hydropower tunnel, raising broader questions about climate justice.
